rationale:
OWNER DECISION 1, 2026-08-18: 'do not switch the handler off for this — write something other than failed'.

THE PROBLEM, plainly. A page whose pages.rebuild_policy is 'owned' belongs to a tool or widget. The owned-page guard in SavePageSectionsAction refuses a generic section save over it, because that save DELETEs and reinserts every page_component and would clobber the live tool. Refusing is correct and is not in question. What is wrong is what the refused work item then RECORDS: it dies `failed`, the same word used for a handler that tried the job and could not do it.

THE RULE THAT MAKES THAT EXPENSIVE. scheduled_tasks.detected-item-promoter (SCH-026; migration 444, corrected by 454 and 465) refuses to dispatch an (item_type, handler_agent) pair whose lifetime successes are under 25% of its terminal outcomes once there are >= 5 of them. Read from the LIVE pre_query on 2026-08-18, that floor is computed over exactly two buckets — c = count FILTER (status IN ('complete','verified')) and f = count FILTER (status = 'failed') — and it names no other status.

HOW THIS CASE MEASURES AGAINST IT. Every ownership refusal is therefore a vote in a competence measure it says nothing about. phantom_internal_link -> page-build-handler is the live illustration: 101 ok / 46 failed = 69% on GENERIC pages, and 0 ok / 14 failed on OWNED ones — not a handler doing badly, a handler never permitted to start. Blended it reads 47%, above the floor today only because its owned rows are a minority. ~134 non-terminal findings sit behind this refusal on owned pages now. When a pair crosses the floor the promoter stops dispatching that item_type ENTIRELY, including the 69% of findings on generic pages that were being repaired. With `wont_fix` the pair reads NEVER TESTED HERE, which is the truth: wont_fix is in neither bucket, so the refusal leaves numerator and denominator alone.

WHY THE CHANGE HAS THE SHAPE IT HAS. An action cannot name its own error step (coordinator.go routeToErrorStep takes a static config value), and a typed Go error does not cross the action -> coordinator -> error_step boundary. The ONLY channel that survives is collected_data.__step_error.message, which routeToErrorStep copies verbatim from the action's error. So the refusal is made machine-identifiable by leading that error with ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix, and the routed step reads it. Scoping to that marker is the load-bearing part: a genuine save failure (shrink guard, banned claim) on the same step still records `failed` and still counts, or the floor would go blind to real incompetence — which is worse than the bug being fixed.

WHY AN OPT-IN FIELD RATHER THAN A RULE IN CODE. Owner ruling 2026-08-02 §2: new authority on a shared seam ships as an opt-in field whose UNSAFE side is the default, so the decision is visible to a reviewer of the CALLER. owned_page_refusal_status is absent everywhere and inert everywhere until a migration names it; one migration (480) names exactly one step.

CONSUMERS, ENUMERATED RATHER THAN ASSERTED (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §3). The refusal can reach a work-item status write only from save_page_sections. Every live agent with such a step, queried 2026-08-18: page-build-handler save_sections -> mark_item_failed (update_work_item_status — this one); page-rerender save_sections -> no error_step at all; tool-recreation-handler save_sections -> complete_error, which runs complete_workflow and writes no item status. One applicable consumer.

BLAST RADIUS OF THE STATUS ITSELF, measured not assumed. Of the consumers that read wont_fix positively: silentCoverageClause (diagnose_silent_check_action.go) treats failed and wont_fix alike; crossLinkFailedStatuses lists both; check_page_canonical_collision's suppression is scoped to its own item_type. No scheduled_task pre_query mentions wont_fix at all. Only retraction differs — workItemClosedStatuses holds wont_fix and not failed, so such a row will not later be retracted, which is correct for a row that is already closed. idx_swi_dedup excludes BOTH, so the dedup key is released either way and the finding re-raises when detected again.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated because it is the obvious objection. It does not repair a single owned page. The repair route (section-editor / apply_section_edit, 220 complete / 5 failed = 98% on owned pages) exists and works; nothing converts a detector's finding into its field_updates payload. That is Tier 2, is architecture-scope, and gets an RFC. This is Tier 1: stop a routing defect from switching off a 69%-effective repair path for findings that have nothing to do with it.

=== ROUND 2 — ANSWERING THE ROUND-1 GATING OBJECTION (editquality). It was RIGHT to ask, and the answer took a query I had not run. ===

THE OBJECTION: this edit writes site_work_items via update_work_item_status inside page-build-handler's own workflow, and two LANDMINES entries say the dispatch loop's mark_complete REPLACES site_work_items.result over a handler's own write — so does edit 2 / migration 480 take effect at all?

I had not checked. I grepped LANDMINES for `wont_fix` consumers and not for `update_work_item_status`, and the entry was there to be found. Recorded in WRONG_CALLS.md.

THE ANSWER, and it is a mixed one. Three code paths write a work item's terminal status after a handler saga:
  (1) CompleteWorkItemAction (load_work_item_actions.go:1017-1025) — guards `AND status NOT IN ('needs_human_review','failed','unresolved','rejected','wont_fix','verified','blocked')`. **`wont_fix` IS in that list**, so mark_complete matches 0 rows and replaces NOTHING — not the status, and not the result either, because both live in the same UPDATE. The landmine is real and does not reach this case.
  (2) failUnverifiedCompletion (complete_work_item_verification.go:428-429) — the IDENTICAL list. Same answer.
  (3) FailWorkItemAction (load_work_item_actions.go:1146-1160) — **NO GUARD AT ALL**: `WHERE id = $1`, nothing else. On this path a handler-written `wont_fix` IS overwritten, to `triaged` or `failed`.

SO: HOW OFTEN DOES A REFUSAL TAKE PATH 3? [MEASURED 2026-08-18] over every page-build-handler item whose error names the guard (`error LIKE '%rebuild_policy=owned%'`), split by `handled_by` — which only fail_work_item and complete_work_item ever write, so NULL means the handler's own write was never touched:
    NULL (handler's own write, untouched)  failed     113
    NULL                                    cancelled    3
    build-dispatch-loop (via fail_work_item) failed       2
**113 of 115 refusals — 98.3% — take the guarded path and the change takes effect. 2 do not**, both on 2026-08-15.

POSITIVE CONTROL, because the above could be read as 'nothing ever overwrites anything': **122 rows carry `status='needs_human_review'` with `handled_by='page-build-handler'`**, most recently today. `needs_human_review` can only come from this handler's own update_work_item_status steps and is in the same guard list as `wont_fix`. That is a handler-set protected status demonstrably surviving this exact loop, 122 times.

WHY TODAY'S DATA COULD NOT HAVE ANSWERED THIS WITHOUT `handled_by`, which is the honest part: both paths currently write `failed`, so the population is indistinguishable on status alone. The 2 rows are visible only because `handled_by` happens to separate the writers. **This change is what makes that overwrite observable at all.**

THE RESIDUAL, STATED RATHER THAN CLOSED: on the ~2% path the item lands `failed` or `triaged` — i.e. exactly today's behaviour, so it is incomplete coverage and not a regression. I have deliberately NOT added the guard to FailWorkItemAction: it is a shared action every dispatch loop reaches, `failed` is itself in the sibling list so a naive copy would stop the retry ladder re-triaging a failed row, and a change to a shared mechanism arriving inside a bug patch is what the 2026-07-28 owner ruling exists to veto. It is contributed instead into `bugs_open/307`, which owns FailWorkItemAction and is actively worked by the `staged_component_build` lane, with the split it probably wants (statuses recording a DECISION protected; `failed`/`unresolved` left overwritable, because that IS the retry ladder).

=== ROUND 3 — ANSWERING ROUND 2. The gating objection was RIGHT and it retracts a claim in this very rationale. ===

**GATING (prior_art_librarian, HIGH): 'nothing converts a detector's finding into its field_updates payload' is a load-bearing absence claim, asserted with no code_check.** Correct, and the seat named the failure mode before I found the instance. **THE CLAIM IS FALSE AND I RETRACT IT.** `copy-editor` is a live, active, non-snapshot agent whose `run_copy_edit` step returns, verbatim from the live prompt: `{"edits":[{"page_component_id":"<id>","slot_name":"<slot>","field_updates":{...},"rationale":"..."}]}` — EXACTLY `apply_section_edit`'s input — built from each component's stored content_data, its rendered HTML AND its declared schema, with the constraints a repair route needs already written (may not introduce a fact or figure; may not drop a link, with the page's required links enumerated as DATA because 'a prose instruction to preserve a set is not reliably followed'; may not change markup; may not change a field's type; may not touch a component not in the list).

WHAT IS TRUE, NARROWED: **nothing routes a specific detector FINDING to that producer** — `copy-editor` takes a page, not a finding, and has no finding input. [MEASURED 2026-08-18] it has **2 orchestration runs in all history, 0 work items, and no scheduled task drives it**, against `section-editor`'s 227 terminal outcomes.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is not cosmetic: **Tier 2 is smaller than this submission said.** Not 'design and build a compute_section_edit action per defect type' but 'aim an existing producer at one finding on one component, and route the five refused types there'. Both ends already exist and work — the applier at 98%, and a producer with a prompt contract someone has already thought hard about. ⚠ And the producer's own near-zero usage is itself a thing to check before building on it: a mechanism nothing drives is the shape this estate keeps mistaking for a missing one, and the shape that turns out to be broken on first real use. **Corrected in place, visibly, in all four places it was load-bearing** — `bugs_open/301` (where I first wrote it), `HANDOFF_2026-08-18c` §2a, `HANDOFF_2026-08-18d`'s Tier 2 sizing, and register WII-019 — plus a WRONG_CALLS entry whose lesson is that I INHERITED the claim from my own lane's handoff and restated it in my own voice with no marker.

**NOTHING IN THIS CHANGE DEPENDS ON THAT CLAIM.** Tier 1 stops a routing defect polluting a competence gate; it was never justified by Tier 2 being large. The retraction makes the follow-on cheaper, not this edit different.

--- the other round-2 objections, each answered by a check rather than an argument ---

**guardian, medium — the new block runs on EVERY call fleet-wide; is it crash-safe for callers who never opted in?** Fair, and behaviourally-inert is not crash-safe. **Seven new test cases added** driving the block with shapes a real payload can carry: `owned_page_refusal_status` as a number / bool / empty string / nil, and `__step_error` as a bare string / an array / with a numeric `message`. All must leave the configured status untouched and must not error. They pass. Mechanically there is no panic path — `config[k].(string)` is a comma-ok assertion, `ExtractNestedFieldString` returns "" for any non-string shape, and `strings.Contains("", marker)` is false — but the tests are what keep that true.

**guardian, low — does anything string-match the CURRENT unprefixed message?** [MEASURED] no. Grepped `rebuild_policy=owned` and `would clobber it` across platform/ internal/ pkg/ cmd/ scripts/ (.go/.py/.sh/.sql): zero non-guard hits. Live `agent_definitions` matching the message: **0**. `scheduled_tasks` matching: **1**, and it is prose inside `held-pair-canary-escalation`'s remedy note (this lane's own), not a predicate.

**debug_historian, medium — the two-active-rows landmine; needs a pre-flight count by version, not the migration's own assertion.** [MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY, before this round] `SELECT id, version, is_active, is_snapshot, deleted_at FROM agent_definitions WHERE type='page-build-handler'` returns **exactly one row, version 1, active, not a snapshot, not deleted**. The landmine does not apply to this type. (The migration's own guard also asserted it and passed at apply — `UPDATE 1` — but the seat is right that a self-assertion is not a pre-flight.)

**debug_historian, medium — no deploy-verification step.** Named now: `kubectl -n ai-persona-system exec <chassis-pod> -- grep -aq 'owned_page_refusal_status' /proc/1/exe` **with a must-be-absent control in the same breath**, never a tag and never `strings` (absent from these images). Then the behavioural check with BOTH controls, which is in RUNBOOK_required_fields_repair.md.

**tooling_provenance, medium — no registry lookup proving UpdateWorkItemStatusAction lives in v3_site_actions.go.** [VERIFIED] `platform/orchestration/actions/registry.go:933` maps `"update_work_item_status"` to `Handler: UpdateWorkItemStatusAction`, and `func UpdateWorkItemStatusAction` is declared at `v3_site_actions.go:5418`. Resolved from the registry, as the rule requires, not from the filename.

**tooling_provenance, low — no doc_notes query for this subject before rewriting its comment.** [MEASURED] the only `doc_notes` rows mentioning `ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix` / `OWNED_PAGE_GUARD` are the LANDMINE entry this same change wrote today (synced under each of its footprints). There is **no prior NOTES entry recording why the comment said 'matched by nothing'**, so the correction is not overwriting someone's reasoning.

**prior_art_librarian, low — 'the key is absent everywhere' is asserted, not checked.** [MEASURED] a `jsonb_each` over every live, non-snapshot, non-deleted `agent_definitions` step returns **exactly one** row carrying `owned_page_refusal_status`: `page-build-handler.mark_item_failed = wont_fix`. Migration 480's own verify block also carries this as a negative control and aborts if it leaks — proven by a probe that planted the key on `image-build-handler` and watched the migration abort naming the leak.

**editquality, medium — captureTextArg may be missing an edit and the test may not compile.** It is defined IN the new test file (edit 4), not in a shared helper; the round-2 sketch simply did not show it. The package suite is green. Its existence is the point of that note: the pre-existing `captureArg` only records a `driver.Value` that is a `string`, and the result payload arrives as `[]byte`, so every JSONB assertion would have passed vacuously against "".

**editquality, low — edit 3 is comment-only and should not count as a mechanism edit.** Agreed, and reframed: it is documentation hygiene REQUIRED by this change rather than a fix of its own. It is included because the comment it corrects (`'It is matched by nothing — the skip protocol is a boolean'`) becomes actively dangerous once the literal decides a terminal status, and a reader who trusts it would rename the constant and silently switch the substitution off.

**editquality, low — the sketch does not confirm validStatuses' scope.** [VERIFIED] `validStatuses` is a local `map[string]bool` declared inside `UpdateWorkItemStatusAction` immediately above the new block, and the new block is placed directly after the existing `if !validStatuses[newStatus]` check, in the same scope. `newStatus` is likewise already declared there.

plan.summary: An owned-page refusal is recorded as `failed`, and a fleet-wide dispatch gate counts `failed`. The detected-item-promoter holds any (item_type, handler_agent) pair whose lifetime successes fall under 25% of complete+verified+failed, and it names no other status — so a routing refusal, which says nothing about the handler's competence, votes against it and can switch the pair off entirely, including on the generic pages where it was working (phantom_internal_link: 69% generic, 0/14 owned). This change makes SavePageSectionsAction's refusal error carry the estate's existing ownership marker, and adds ONE opt-in config key to update_work_item_status — owned_page_refusal_status, absent and therefore inert everywhere — which records that status instead when the routed step error carries the marker. A genuine save failure on the same step still records `failed` and still counts. Migration 480 opts exactly one step in (page-build-handler.mark_item_failed -> wont_fix); it is applied and ledger-recorded, and is inert on the current binary because nothing reads the key until the Go half rolls.

edits.rationale: Make the ownership refusal machine-identifiable at the only place its terminal status is chosen. routeToErrorStep copies the error message verbatim into __step_error.message; without a marker in it, an ownership refusal and a shrink-guard failure are the same string to the routed step. Uses the estate's existing single ownership token rather than inventing a second one.
edits.sketch:
@@ owned-page guard, the refusal return @@
-			return nil, fmt.Errorf(
-				"page %s is rebuild_policy=owned (tool/widget-owned): a generic section save "+
+			// The error LEADS with ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix (owner decision 1,
+			// 2026-08-18). routeToErrorStep copies this message verbatim into
+			// collected_data.__step_error.message, which is the only channel that
+			// survives the action -> coordinator -> error_step boundary.
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf(
+				"%s: page %s is rebuild_policy=owned (tool/widget-owned): a generic section save "+
 					"would clobber it. Use apply_section_edit for targeted edits or the tool "+
 					"pipeline for rebuilds. Refusing to overwrite.",
-				pageName)
+				ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix, pageName)

edits.rationale: The opt-in itself, on UpdateWorkItemStatusAction. Absent -> inert -> today's behaviour for every caller (the unsafe default is OFF, per the 2026-08-02 §2 ruling). Present AND the routed error carries the ownership marker -> record the refusal status instead. Scoped to the marker so a genuine save failure still counts in the promoter's floor. Validated against the SAME validStatuses map as `status`, because two vocabularies for one column is the drift class this estate keeps filing bugs about.

DOCUMENTATION HYGIENE REQUIRED BY THIS CHANGE, not a fix of its own (editquality, round 2 — reframed as asked). The comment read 'It is matched by nothing — the skip protocol is a boolean'. That was already false when written (two call sites match it in an upstream skip_reason) and becomes actively dangerous here: the literal now decides a work item's TERMINAL STATUS, so a reader who trusts the comment would rename the constant and silently switch the substitution off, with nothing erroring anywhere. [MEASURED] no doc_notes row records why it said that, so nothing is being overwritten. The full matcher set is listed so a future edit can see what a rename costs, and the test builds its fixture FROM the constant so a rename goes RED.
edits.sketch:
-// ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix marks a skip caused by this guard. It is matched by
-// nothing — the skip protocol is a boolean — but it is the string to pod-grep ...
+// ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix marks a refusal caused by this guard. ...
+// > **CORRECTED 2026-08-18:** this comment used to say "It is matched by nothing".
+// > ... The full matcher set, so a future edit knows what it would break:
+// >	 SavePageSectionsAction     — an upstream skip_reason, and its own error
+// >	 UpdatePageStatusAction     — an upstream skip_reason (refuses the 'deployed' stamp)
+// >	 UpdateWorkItemStatusAction — __step_error.message (chooses the terminal status)
+// > Changing this literal changes an item's terminal STATUS, not only a log line.
 const ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix = "OWNED_PAGE_GUARD"

edits.rationale: Eleven cases, in three groups, and the groups are what make it a control rather than a demonstration. (a) The downgrade fires on an ownership refusal. (b) The DISCRIMINATION cases — field absent, and a genuine shrink-guard failure on the same step — without which this passes on an implementation that marks every failure wont_fix and blinds the promoter's floor to real incompetence, which is worse than the bug. (c) NEW IN ROUND 3, for the guardian's medium: seven crash-safety cases driving the block with shapes a real payload can carry (`owned_page_refusal_status` as number/bool/empty/nil; `__step_error` as a bare string, an array, or with a numeric message), each required to leave the configured status untouched and not error — because this block runs on EVERY call to a shared action, and behaviourally-inert is not the same as crash-safe. captureTextArg is defined in this file: the pre-existing captureArg records only a string driver.Value and the result payload arrives as []byte, so every JSONB assertion would otherwise pass vacuously against "". Mutation-proven both ways: a marker that never matches fails the downgrade assertion; one that always matches fails the default-OFF and genuine-failure assertions.

The config half: the single deliberate opt-in. Guarded on the live step's shape (exactly one live row; action is update_work_item_status; status is still 'failed'; the key is not already set; save_sections actually routes its error HERE, or the field would sit on a step the refusal never reaches and the migration would look applied and do nothing). Verify is a DO/RAISE block, not SELECTs — ON_ERROR_STOP does not fire on a non-empty result set — and carries a negative control asserting no OTHER live step acquired the key, without which the positive assertion would pass identically on an UPDATE with no WHERE clause. Exercised end to end before applying: dry run in a transaction that rolled back, plus two probes proving the already-set guard and the leak control each abort.
edits.sketch:
UPDATE agent_definitions
   SET default_config = jsonb_set(default_config,
           '{workflow,steps,mark_item_failed,config,owned_page_refusal_status}',
           '"wont_fix"'::jsonb, true)
 WHERE type = 'page-build-handler' AND is_active
   AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL;

edits.rationale: Removes the key and asserts the rest of the step survived (a #- on the wrong path would otherwise look like a clean rollback). Deliberately does NOT rewrite rows already written wont_fix back to failed: they are a true record of a refusal that happened, and rewriting them would re-inject exactly the false votes 480 removed. Names the query that finds them (result ? 'owned_page_refusal') for anyone who disagrees.

grounded_in: LIVE scheduled_tasks.detected-item-promoter pre_query, read 2026-08-18: "SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE h.status IN ('complete', 'verified')) AS c, count(*) FILTER (WHERE h.status = 'failed') AS f" and "SELECT (c + f) < 5 OR c >= 0.25 * (c + f)" — the floor names no status other than complete/verified/failed.

LIVE pg_indexes idx_swi_dedup, read 2026-08-18: "WHERE ((item_key IS NOT NULL) AND (status <> ALL (ARRAY['complete','verified','rejected','wont_fix','failed','unresolved','cancelled'])))" — both failed and wont_fix release the dedup key.

LIVE agent_definitions page-build-handler mark_item_failed, read 2026-08-18: {"action": "update_work_item_status", "config": {"status": "failed", "skip_if_missing": true, "work_item_id_field": "input_data.work_item_id"}} — an unconditional failed.

LIVE agent_definitions, every live step whose action is save_page_sections, read 2026-08-18: page-build-handler.save_sections -> mark_item_failed; page-rerender.save_sections -> (no error_step); tool-recreation-handler.save_sections -> complete_error (action complete_workflow).

plan.risks:
6. **[ROUND 1 GATING OBJECTION, ANSWERED WITH EVIDENCE AND A STATED RESIDUAL]** `FailWorkItemAction` has no terminal-status guard, unlike its two siblings, so on the loop's error path a handler-written `wont_fix` is overwritten to `triaged`/`failed`. [MEASURED 2026-08-18] that path carries 2 of 115 owned-page refusals (1.7%); the other 113 have `handled_by IS NULL`, meaning the handler's own write stood. Positive control: 122 `needs_human_review` rows with `handled_by='page-build-handler'` prove a protected status survives this loop. The residual is today's behaviour, not a regression. NOT fixed here on purpose — shared action, fleet-wide retry semantics, 2026-07-28 ruling. Contributed to `bugs_open/307`, which owns that function.

1. The status substitution is keyed on a STRING MARKER in __step_error.message, because an action cannot name its own error step and a typed error does not survive the coordinator boundary. If someone renames ownedPageSkipReasonPrefix, refusals silently go back to `failed`. Mitigated by the corrected doc comment listing all three matchers and by the test building its fixture FROM the constant, so a rename breaks the test rather than production. A reviewer should say whether a marker is acceptable here or whether the coordinator should carry structured error metadata instead — that is the wider fix and it is not in this change.

2. `wont_fix` differs from `failed` in exactly one consumer: workItemClosedStatuses (retraction) holds wont_fix and not failed, so these rows will never be retracted. Argued as correct for an already-closed row. A reviewer should check whether any consumer this lane did not find reads wont_fix as 'a HUMAN ruled on this' — check_page_canonical_collision does, but scoped to its own item_type.

3. It narrows what the promoter's floor can see. That is the intent, but it means an owned-page refusal no longer shows up as a failure anywhere the floor looks. The visibility channel is the owned_page_review row that bugs_closed/295 already files, plus result->'owned_page_refusal' on the item. A reviewer should check that is enough, because the alternative reading is that this hides a real routing defect.

4. It repairs nothing. ~134 findings stay queued on owned pages; the detector->editor routing (Tier 2) is architecture-scope and gets an RFC. If a reviewer thinks Tier 1 makes Tier 2 less likely to be built, say so.

5. Coordination: bugs_open/301's author is reordering the SAME guard in the same week (moving it earlier so the LLM writer does not run first). These changes compose — an earlier refusal still terminates the item and still needs to write something other than failed — but a reviewer should confirm the marker survives whatever step 301 moves the refusal to.
